brief.headline: Ask for ₹28.69 L in savings by matching the best prices we already pay to Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic

priceAsk.summary: Cut prices on the three big items to match our cheapest supplier — Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic
priceAsk.target: Save ₹28.69 L per year across rigid plastic packaging; the PP cap alone is ₹14.05 L (cut ₹1.08 to ₹0.81 per piece); the HDPE bottle is ₹7.88 L (₹1.53 to ₹1.38); the measuring cup is ₹6.75 L (₹0.46 to ₹0.35)
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Mars Plastics ₹0.81 for the same PP cap — Cincorp charges ₹1.08 (33.2% more). Same story on the bottle (10.7% more) and cup (30.6% more vs Premier Plastic). The open market puts the 28 mm cap typically at ₹0.85–0.95 per piece, so our ₹0.81 benchmark is tight but fair. Tell them we're holding all suppliers to the best price we pay.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 60 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹16.02 L in cash for us if we go to 30 days; another ₹8.01 L if we push to 15 days more (total 60 days would be ₹24.03 L). Start by asking for 60.

brief.financialLeverage: They're a tiny shop — ₹4.11 Cr in sales — and we're huge to them: our ₹1.95 Cr is 47.43% of everything they sell. They keep only 6.0% of every ₹100 they make, way below similar firms (15.0%), so every rupee matters to them. They already owe 1.13 times their own cash and their cash is stuck for 101 days (a bit faster than rivals at 107 days, but still tight). Their health score is C (51/100) and the distress zone is grey (1.83), so they're under strain — but they borrow at only 4.54%, cheap enough that faster payment is worth real money to them. Bottom line: we're nearly half their business, so we have the muscle to ask for both a price cut and longer payment — but layer the asks (price first, then terms) so we don't tip a fragile supplier into trouble.

evidence.point: They keep far less profit than competitors
The PP cap is 33.2% above our best price
evidence.figure: We pay Cincorp ₹1.08/NOS; Mars Plastics charges ₹0.81/NOS; gap 33.2%; costs us ₹14.05 L extra per year

evidence.point: They owe more than they own
Their cash is tied up for 101 days
evidence.figure: Cash stuck 101 days (they wait 88 days to collect, pay suppliers in 39 days); peers average 107 days

evidence.point: Health score flags them as strained but not critical
evidence.figure: Health C (51/100); distress zone grey (Altman Z 1.83); small entity under ₹10 Cr

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B (65/100), does pharma bottles and caps; top second-source candidate already qualified for packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) with pharma containers and closures; robust alternate already qualified for packaging

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India plastic manufacturer found by public search, medium confidence; not yet qualified or priced

risks: They're in the grey distress zone (1.83) and keep very thin profit (6.0%) — pushing too hard on price and payment together could break them; layer the asks and watch for supply hiccups
We're nearly half their sales (47.43%) — if they stumble, we lose a big chunk of our rigid-plastic supply; have Manjushree or Mold-Tek ready as backups before you squeeze
The market ask for the 28 mm cap is ₹0.85–0.95 typical, so our ₹0.81 benchmark from Mars is already tight — they may push back hard; be ready to meet in the middle around ₹0.85
Small entity under ₹10 Cr flagged as 'verify' — double-check their capacity and quality before leaning on them for the full ₹28.69 L saving
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying you ₹28.69 lakh more each year than our best suppliers for the same rigid plastic items — let's work together to close that gap and keep the volume with you.
